observations: Photo shows a V8-style engine with a transmission bolted directly below/behind it, sitting on bare dirt in what looks like an outdoor used-parts yard.
Other partial engines/assemblies are visible in the background on both sides, suggesting a parts dealer's lot.
A watermark reading 'BLESSED CHILD' is overlaid on the image.
No engine code, casting number, VIN plate, or identification sticker is legible anywhere on the block, head, or bell housing.
Wiring harness and some hoses are attached and appear intact, but connectors and sensor completeness cannot be fully traced from this single angle.
No fluids, rust, cracks, or oil seepage can be assessed in detail at this resolution.

identity.kind: V8 engine with transmission (gearbox) assembly, seller-claimed Lexus/Toyota 3UR-FE type

claims.evidence: No Lexus badge, VIN tag, or vehicle-specific marking visible anywhere in photo 0.
No engine code stamp, casting number, or ID sticker is legible on the block or head in photo 0.

claims.claim: Implied that engine and gearbox are a matched, complete pulled set
claims.evidence: They appear physically joined in the photo, but no documentation or tag ties them to a specific donor vehicle.

risks.risk: Engine code cannot be confirmed as genuine 3UR-V8, so the item could be a different (cheaper) V8 passed off under this name.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the stamped engine code/casting number on the block, or the engine ID sticker/plate.
risks.if_unproven: priced as an unidentified/generic used V8, not as a confirmed Lexus 3UR-V8

risks.risk: Running condition is unknown; a stationary yard photo gives no evidence the engine starts, holds compression, or is free of internal damage.
risks.proof: Video clip of the engine cranking/running with audible sound, plus oil on the dipstick.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for-parts condition

risks.risk: Mileage and internal wear cannot be seen.
risks.proof: Odometer photo from the donor vehicle or a mileage sticker/service record.

risks.risk: Completeness of ancillaries (sensors, actuators, ECU, wiring loom ends) cannot be confirmed from one angle; missing parts raise cost to make it usable.
risks.proof: Photos from all four sides and the underside showing connector ends and sensor presence.
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete, with the cost of missing sensors/harness ends to be added

risks.risk: No evidence engine and transmission are a matched pair from the same donor car (mismatched units are common in parts yards and can cause fitment issues).
risks.proof: A single photo showing matching chassis tag or donor vehicle ID connecting the engine and gearbox serials.
risks.if_unproven: priced as separately sourced engine and gearbox, not as a verified matched set

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/casting stamp or ID sticker on the block or head.
Video clip of the engine cranking or running with sound.
Photos of all four sides and underside showing connectors, sensors, and harness completeness.
Any donor-vehicle documentation (VIN tag, service sticker) linking engine and gearbox as a matched set.
response.reason: The engine code that would confirm this is actually a 3UR-V8 Lexus unit (and thus set its market value) is not legible anywhere in the photo, so even a worst-case price cannot be anchored to the right comparable class without that shot.
